title: Unified Osculator Theorem: Merge Positive and Negative Cases

problemStatement.formal: theorem unified_osculator (d : ℕ) (c : ℤ) (n : ℕ) (hcop : IsCoprime (d : ℤ) 10) (hc : (d : ℤ) ∣ 10 * c - 1) : (d : ℤ) ∣ n ↔ (d : ℤ) ∣ (↑(n / 10) + c * ↑(n % 10))
problemStatement.plain: Can the positive and negative osculator theorems be merged into a single theorem with a signed osculator c in Z? YES - the negative case is the positive case with c replaced by -c.
whyMatters: Simplifies the divisibility truncation framework from two theorems to one
Reveals structural relationship between positive and negative osculators
Makes the framework easier to extend to other bases

proven: unified_osculator: single theorem subsumes both positive and negative cases
neg_osculator_from_unified: negative case derived as corollary via c -> -c
dual_osculators_sum: d | (c_pos + c_neg) for dual osculators
knownResults.goal: Merge positive and negative osculator theorems into one

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETED: Unified osculator theorem fully proved (0 sorries). Gallery entry created. The key insight is sign absorption: d | (10*c_neg + 1) iff d | (10*(-c_neg) - 1), so the negative case is simply the positive case with negated osculator.
builtItems: src/data/proofs/divisibility-truncation-general-oq-01/ - Gallery entry with meta.json, annotations.json, index.ts
insights: The negative osculator is not independent - it is the positive case with c negated
Sign absorption: d | (10c+1) iff d | (10(-c)-1) reduces two theorems to one
Dual osculator sum: c_pos + c_neg is always divisible by d (follows from summing osculator conditions)
For minimal osculators, c_pos + c_neg = d exactly (e.g., 5+2=7, 4+9=13)

approaches.name: Sign absorption
approaches.description: Use unified_osculator with negative c to derive negative osculator case
